items.excerpt: HarperCollins CEO Brian Murray says publishers, agents and authors need a shared set of best practices for AI-written books, warning that books written with AI "could very well be considered uncopyrightable." He argues detection software is not the answer — human-authorship verification standards are.

Nigerian author Jerry Adedayo Falade's debut was pulled after six- and seven-figure deals over AI allegations; he offers 2021 text messages predating ChatGPT as proof of authorship. PW examines the acquisition process that could not verify how the manuscript was made — and the racial-bias pattern Falade points to.

At the Media Transformation Summit, publishers described how AI has collapsed production barriers — faster audiobooks, faster format adaptation — while the hard decisions of what to publish and for whom remain untouched. A working portrait of where AI actually lands in the publishing pipeline.

Digital Science has launched Papers AI, an AI-native workspace where researchers write, organise notes and analyse data with a context-aware assistant across the whole project. Built by the Overleaf team, it surfaces AI-suggested edits users review before accepting.

Pope Leo XIV's 42,000-word encyclical is being read across publishing as one of the most cogent ethical frameworks yet for AI — covering regulatory gaps, data monopolies, environmental cost and workforce impact. Andrew Albanese asks whether it can actually move AI regulation.

This week's roundup notes that South Korean readers in their 20s and 30s — the heaviest generative-AI users at 75.3% and 71.1% — are simultaneously driving a reading revival, some using AI to answer questions and recommend books, others using books as a counterweight to AI.

Wendy Queen and Jonathan Woahn argue scholarly publishing keeps building the foundations and letting others own the layer above — and that AI is the third such moment. If the community does not shape how AI participates in scholarship now, commercial platforms will decide.

ALLi unpacks the viral study of 14,419 self-published Amazon titles that found more than a quarter show signs of AI use. AI-flagged books sold less than human-written ones but still made meaningful money — a market signal indie authors now have to plan around.

AI search engine Perplexity is opening its own ebook store, aiming to convert hundreds of millions of answer-engine users into book buyers via publishers and distributors. Indie authors would reach it through aggregators like Draft2Digital and PublishDrive.

A Stony Brook University study using the Pangram detector found roughly one in five of 14,000 sampled Kindle ebooks contained substantial AI text — including BookTok sensation Daggermouth at about 60%, which the author denies.
생성형 AI가 번역·집필·오디오북 제작까지 파고들면서 한국 출판계가 'AI 표시' 논쟁에 휩싸였다. 한 출판사는 'Human Authored' 인증제를 도입했지만, 업계 전반에는 표기 기준도 검증 절차도 아직 없다.
전자책 앱 '책도둑'이 AI 번역 사실을 뒤늦게 밝히며 논란이 커졌다. 번역계는 "AI는 유능한 조수가 될 수 있지만 근본적인 판단과 선택은 번역가의 몫"이라며 활용 범위와 공개 기준을 세워야 한다고 지적한다.
'평생소장 고전'을 내건 전자책 앱 '책도둑'이 결제 과정에서 AI 번역 사용을 알리지 않아 이용자 반발을 샀다. 운영자는 25일 SNS에서 "AI를 쓴다. 대신 말도 안 되는 가격으로 책을 드린다"고 밝혔다.
1만9800원에 고전 700여 권을 평생 소장한다던 전자책 앱이 AI 번역을 숨긴 사실이 드러나 전액 환불에 나섰다. AI 번역 고지 의무를 둘러싼 소비자 신뢰 문제가 한국 출판 시장의 쟁점으로 떠올랐다.
